summary: Specializing in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy, Koichi Takahashi earned his PhD from the University of Tokyo in 2004 under Yasunori Ejima and Akira Saitō. He held posts at the University of Tokyo as an assistant, project researcher, and professor.

Koichi Yokoyama studied Buddhist studies and philosophy, earning an MA from the University of Tokyo (~1968–1970) under Akira Hirakawa and studying under Gyoin Hashimoto in 1970. He served as an assistant professor at Rikkyo University (~1974–2006).
Focusing on Buddhist and religious studies, Koin Takada studied under Gyoin Hashimoto (~1937–1953), whom he succeeded in 1967. He also studied at Ryukoku University (~1941–1944).

Working in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics, Koji Kamioka studied under Yutaka Ochihara and at Kyoto University (~1957–1963). He was a lecturer at Kyoto Sangyo University (1969) and a researcher at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1972–2004).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Koji Takahashi studied at Otani University (~1953–1957) and earned a doctorate from Bukkyo University by 1991. He served Bukkyo University as an assistant professor (~1969–1979) and professor (~1979–2004).

Kojun Fukui worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies, studying under Sokichi Tsuda and earning a doctorate from Waseda University. He was a professor at Waseda University (1941–1969) and president of Taisho University (1928–1968, 1972–1975).
A scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies, Kojun Saito studied under Seiren Matsunami. He served as a lecturer at Taisho University (attested 1965).
Kokan Fujita is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Yujun Endo. He served as a professor at Koyasan University (attested 1995–2002).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Koken Sasaki studied at Rissho University (~1950–1960). He spent his career at Rissho University as an assistant professor, department chair (~1977–2002), professor and director (2000), and professor emeritus (~2002), and taught Guohui Shi.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Koki Kawagishi served as a professor at both Eizan Gakuin and Shitennoji University (both attested 1976).

Konan Naito specialized in Sinology and history and archaeology. After studying at Akita Normal School (~1881–1885), he served on the faculty at Kyoto University (~1907–1926) and taught Taichiro Kobayashi.
Konchok Drakpa studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Thubten Chökyi Dorje. He taught Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.
Konchok Gyatso, a Tibetology scholar, studied under Sherab Gyatso. He held an attested position at the Tibetan Academy of Social Sciences in 2014.
Konchok Tenpai Gyeltsen studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.
Konchok Yeshe Ozer studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Thubten Chökyi Dorje.

Working in Indology and Tibetology, Konrad Klaus studied at Göttingen and Marburg under Michael Hahn. Between 1999 and 2001, he held acting professorships at Bochum, Marburg, and Bonn, succeeding Claus Vogel in 2001, and taught Bruno Galasek.
A scholar in Buddhist studies, Kosai Fukushima held posts at Otani University as dean of students (attested 1985) and professor (attested 1992). He taught Paul L. Swanson.

Specializing in history, archaeology, Sinology, and Japanology, Kosaku Hamada studied at the University of Tokyo (~1901–1905). He taught at the University of Tokyo (~1909–1913) and Kyoto University (~1913–1938), and taught Taichiro Kobayashi and Seiichi Mizuno.

Kosei Ishii specialized in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, earning a doctorate from Waseda University under Akira Hirakawa. He held teaching posts at Waseda, Komazawa Junior College (1994–2006), and Komazawa University as professor of Buddhism (2006–2021).

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Kosei Tada studied at the University of Tokyo (~1957–1961). He held posts at Taisho University (~1985–2009) and the Society for the Study of Buddhist Culture (attested 2004).
